abstract: An ideal quantum walk transitions from one vertex to another with perfect fidelity, but in physical systems, the particle may be hindered by potential energy barriers. Then the particle has some amplitude of tunneling through the barriers, and some amplitude of staying put. We investigate the algorithmic consequence of such barriers for the quantum walk formulation of Grover’s algorithm. We prove that the failure amplitude must scale as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ for search to retain its quantum $O(\sqrt{N})$ runtime; otherwise, it searches in classical $O(N)$ time. Thus searching larger “databases” requires increasingly reliable hop operations or error correction. This condition holds for both discrete- and continuous-time quantum walks.

specification.problem: Determine how the failure amplitude of hop operations (amplitude of staying put instead of hopping through a potential barrier) in the quantum walk formulation of Grover search affects runtime: the failure amplitude must scale as O(1/sqrt(N)) to retain O(sqrt(N)) search time, otherwise runtime degrades to classical O(N).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the scaling condition on hop failure amplitude for quantum-walk Grover search (discrete- and continuous-time). The detailed walk operators, proof, and circuits are not given in the abstract, so only the scaling relations are specified.

equations.label: Failure amplitude condition
equations.description: Condition on hop failure amplitude for the search to keep quantum speedup
equations.abstract_quote: the failure amplitude must scale as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract as a necessary scaling condition.

equations.label: Quantum runtime
equations.description: Retained quantum search runtime when the condition holds
equations.justification: Abstract states the quantum runtime is O(sqrt(N)).

equations.description: Runtime when failure amplitude is too large
equations.justification: Abstract states the fallback runtime is classical O(N).

registers.role: Optional coin/direction register for a discrete-time walk; absent in continuous-time

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over all N vertices (assumed standard walk-search start).

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition over vertices.
Repeat walk steps: apply a marked-vertex oracle/perturbation, then a hop operator that succeeds with amplitude ~1 and fails (stays put) with amplitude epsilon, for T steps or evolution time.
If epsilon is not O(1/sqrt(N)), the hop errors accumulate and the search needs T = O(N) steps.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after the walk runs for time T, measure the vertex register in the computational basis to read out the marked vertex. The abstract does not specify the measurement.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: check whether the measured vertex is marked using the oracle or a classical check; if not, repeat the run. Not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Symbol epsilon is introduced for the failure amplitude.
Register sizes and the initial state are assumed from the standard quantum-walk search setup, not stated in the abstract.
Standard uniform-superposition initial state and log2 N qubit vertex register.
Measurement is a computational-basis readout of the vertex register, with classical verification and repetition (assumed).
